criteria.criterion: The stated objective is implemented: Show me, for one engineering job, every developer attempt that was made and what each one cost, so I can tell whether an automated run is converging or thrashing without reading the whole history.
criteria.evidence_ref: company/engineering/attempt_ledger.py:build_attempt_ledger joins EngineeringStore, ExecutionStore and ResourceUsageStore to produce AttemptLedger with per-attempt entries (outcome, input/output/total units, duration, reasoning class) and aggregate totals. Tests at tests/test_company_engineering_execution.py:1648-1757 cover single-attempt, multi-attempt correction loop, empty-before-session, and unknown-order error cases.

findings.summary: attempt_ledger.py imports Mapping (line 17), Outcome (line 23) and JobState (line 28) but none are referenced in the module body.
In __init__.py __all__, AttemptLedger and AttemptLedgerEntry are inserted between ALLOWED_CEILINGS and ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS, which breaks the existing ASCII sort order (ALLOWED_T < Attempt in ASCII).

Usage records are correlated to attempts by enumerate index+1, not by an explicit attempt field on the usage record; a gap or reorder in the usage store would mis-correlate (the implementer flagged this).

notes: The work is purely additive: one new read-only module, its re-export, and five new tests. No existing behaviour was modified. The three unused imports are harmless but should be cleaned up. The sequence-correlation assumption is real but inherited from the store design (usage records have no explicit attempt field); the implementer correctly disclosed it.
